verdicts.evidence: lines 587-604, 722-723, 730, 764-786, 823, 849-865: every button has a listener that calls the api or changes the view; day links, list-link and nav get real hash hrefs (514-515, 537-538) handled by onRoute (899-930).

lines 561-566, 687-689: list and job come from api.listJobs/getJob; counts at 543-547 are computed from the loaded jobs; empty and failed cases say so (535, 575). No hardcoded sample values or placeholder text.
line 853: the confirm dialog title is rewritten to name the job reference and customer; the move form (310-321) sits on the job page under the current date and slot (657).

lines 444-446, 726-727: note text is written to sessionStorage per job on every input and restored at 715 on return or reload; on a failed save the value is not cleared (752-757); draft cleared only on success (745).
line 857: dialog focus starts on 'Keep job open', so Enter does not complete. Move date preselects the next day (770) inside a form the user opened; nothing irreversible runs by default.
List view shows the day's jobs sorted by slot with inline search (527-529, 593-598); adding a note is an inline form on the job page (332-340). Only the irreversible complete action takes a dialog.

Contents are list, search, job facts, notes, add note, move, complete (246-344). Day links (250-251) let a moved job be found on its new day; phone is part of the customer record; count line 547 is the list state. No unrelated panels.
line 306: 'Complete job' is the only .primary in the job view; move, cancel, save note are plain .btn (307, 317-318, 337). Dialog has one primary (353) and one plain (352). List view has no primary.

Completing cannot be reversed (349), yet line 353 gives 'Complete job and send invoice' class 'btn primary' in the dialog and line 306 styles 'Complete job' as the primary beside the frequent Move action. Focus on cancel (857) does not change the styling.

lines 607-622: buttons get aria-disabled only while their own request runs, with a busy label; cancel is inert only during the complete request (619). For a complete job the actions row is hidden (664) and the state reads Complete.
No title attributes, tooltips or hover cards anywhere in the markup or script (lines 233-357, 409-937).
All visible strings (lines 235-353, 438-442, 535-575, 697-703, 754-756, 806-891) concern jobs, notes, moves and connection problems. No mention of implementation, mock data or unfinished features.

Only notices: 'Tomorrow or later.' under the date label (312), 'Once moved, this job cannot be put back on today.' above Move job and shown only when it applies (315, 771), and the dialog consequence line (349). Each sits at its decision.

No sentence narrates the screen. Text is headings, field labels (256, 311, 333), one hint at the date field (312) and error text; 'Your note is still in the box. Save it again.' (756) is recovery guidance at the control.

Subtitle under 'Today's jobs' is the date (513), not a restatement; 'New date' has the rule 'Tomorrow or later.' (311-312); dialog title names the job and its body states the consequence (348-349, 853).
Headings are 'Today's jobs', 'Jobs for <date>', customer name, 'Notes' (510, 652, 326). No greetings, slogans, exclamation marks or promotional words in any string.

Buttons: 'Try again', 'Clear search', 'Undo move', 'Complete job', 'Move to another day', 'Move job', 'Cancel', 'Save note', 'Keep job open', 'Complete job and send invoice' (262-353). 'Previous day'/'Next day' are nav links (250-251).

line 486 maps status to 'Complete'/'Booked'; dates formatted by Intl (418-425); error codes mapped to plain sentences (438-442). Job id appears only in the URL (451), the label shows the HH reference.

lines 438-442 turn ECONNRESET into 'The connection dropped.'; messages read 'Could not load the jobs. ...' with Try again (575-577), 'The note was not saved. ... Save it again.' (756), 'The job was not moved. ... Try again.' (818). No raw codes.

Error wording is 'Could not load', 'was not saved', 'was not moved', 'Choose a date after today.', 'Write the note before saving.' (575, 737, 756, 794, 818). No 'failed', 'invalid', 'oops', capitals or exclamation marks.
lines 534-538: zero jobs shows 'No jobs booked for today.' with a 'See tomorrow's jobs' (or 'Go to today's jobs') link button. Notes show 'No notes yet.' (627) directly above the add-note form.

Nothing booked: message plus day link (534-538). Search with no match: 'No jobs today match "x".' plus Clear search (539-541). Load failure: 'Could not load the jobs.' in role=alert plus Try again (573-577).

List failure shows alert and retry, keeping the earlier list with its time (569-577); job and notes failures have alert and retry (698-704); note, move and complete failures state it beside the control and keep the input (756, 818, 889-891).

lines 557-558: 'Loading jobs...' and placeholder rows at once; 'Loading job...' (684), 'Loading notes...' (679); submit buttons switch to 'Saving note...', 'Moving job...', 'Completing job...' (615-618). Calls end within 1.5 s.

With no cached list, status is set to 'Loading jobs...' and the empty-state link and clear button are hidden (555-558); empty text is written only in renderList after data arrives (534). Notes show 'Loading notes...' until loaded (679, 626).

overflow-wrap: anywhere on rows, h1, facts, notes and dialog title (90, 153, 177, 203, 213); grid tracks use minmax(0, 1fr) (150, 219); buttons wrap in flex rows (183, 193); the list renders any count (529). No field is left to print undefined.
The note is the only explicit-save edit of substance; it is stored per job on input (727) and put back into the box when the job is reopened or the page reloads (715).
line 312: 'Tomorrow or later.' is shown under the 'New date' label before any input and tied by aria-describedby (313); min is also set on the date input (769).
Each form has a single field (search 257, date 313, note 334); the note and move forms have only a required field, so no form mixes required and optional fields.

Validation runs only in the submit handlers (736-741, 793-795). The input handler only clears an existing error once text is present (728); the date error clears on change (785). Nothing reports an error during typing.
note-error sits directly under the textarea (335) and move-error under the date input (314); invalid fields get a 2px border via aria-invalid (138) plus the text message (737-738, 781-782).
The note value is cleared only on success (747); on any failure the textarea keeps its text (752-757). The move form stays open with its chosen date on failure (809-818).

lines 737-739 and 780-784 set the error text, aria-invalid and focus on the field; the fields reference their error by aria-describedby (313, 334). Server failures go into role=alert regions (320, 339).

Submit buttons carry no disabled attribute (317, 337); aria-disabled is set only while their request runs (607-617). Submitting an empty note or bad date shows 'Write the note before saving.' or 'Choose a date.' (737, 793).

Each handler returns early if its key is in the busy set (733, 789, 825, 867), adds the key before the call (742, 798, 828, 869), and the button label changes to a busy label (615-618) until the finally block.

syncBusy runs synchronously before each await and swaps the button label (742, 798, 828, 869, 607-618); retry clears the alert and shows loading (554-558); search filters on input (593-598); route changes swap views at once (905-906).

Saved note appears in the list and the box clears (744-750); move updates the date line and status text (805-806); complete flips the state and shows a message (876-883); every failure writes an alert (756, 818, 889-891).

The complete message reports the emailed invoice, not otherwise visible (883). 'Moved to <date>, <slot>.' (806) repeats the date line updated in place (657) but is also the anchor for Undo move; two readings of the rule gave different verdicts.

All errors are written into in-place role=alert paragraphs (267, 277, 303, 320, 328, 339, 350) and cleared only on retry or success; there are no timers that remove messages. The Undo move button stays with the status line (302, 666).

Move runs with no confirmation dialog (786-808) and sets undo with an 'Undo move' button when the server can restore it (801, 666, 823-836); where it cannot (moving off today) a line at the button says so (315, 771).

line 853 titles the dialog 'Complete <ref> for <customer>?'; body says the invoice is emailed at once and 'This cannot be reversed.' (349); buttons are 'Keep job open' and 'Complete job and send invoice' (352-353); focus starts on Keep (857).

The only confirmation dialog is complete-dialog (347-355), opened solely by Complete job (849-858), an irreversible action that emails an invoice. Move, save note, cancel and clear search run without confirmation.
No optimistic updates: note, move, undo and complete all await the api and render from the returned job (744, 800, 830, 881). Search is client-side only.
The one modal holds a single decision with two buttons (347-355) and opens only when the user presses Complete job (849-856). Move and add note are inline forms on the page, not modals.

Native dialog opened with showModal() (856) and focus set inside (857); Escape closes via the native cancel event except mid-request (863); the close handler returns focus to the opener (864); 'Keep job open' is a visible cancel (352).

List view is heading, date, day links, search, then the jobs list (244-271) with nothing decorative above it. Job view leads with 'What needs doing' in the largest text (290-291, 178), then address, phone, actions, notes.
After a 56px top bar (233-240) the page opens on the h1 'Today's jobs' and the list controls (244-271). No hero, greeting or introductory panel.
The only summary is one text line 'N jobs, M complete' (546-547), which tells the engineer how much of the day is left; with a search it becomes the match count (543). No cards or charts.

With a search active the status reads 'X of Y jobs match "q".' next to a Clear search button (542-544, 262); a no-match search also shows Clear search (539-541). The day shown is named in the heading (510).

All controls are native a, button, input, textarea and dialog elements (237-353); job rows are links (491-492); busy buttons use aria-disabled so stay focusable (610); focus is managed after actions (739, 807, 857, 917, 925).

Status is the word 'Complete' with a check icon or 'Booked' (481-487); errors are text with a left border (97-100); invalid fields get a thicker border and a message (138, 737); current nav has an underline bar (84-87).

Status and alert regions exist in the markup before use: role=status at 261, 275, 301, 327, 357 and role=alert at 267, 277, 303, 320, 328, 339, 350; busy labels and 'Note saved.' go through the sr status region (443, 608, 750).
line 307: the Move to another day button has aria-expanded and aria-controls; it is set to true on open (773) and false in closeMove (646).

Viewport meta (5); phone-first CSS with rows as a three-column wrapping grid (149-154), inputs at 100% width (130), wrapping action rows (183, 193), dialog width calc(100% - 32px) with stacked buttons (208, 215). Desktop layout only from 48rem (217).
lines 907-908 set aria-current=page on the 'Today's jobs' nav link when today's list is shown and remove it otherwise; CSS 84-87 marks it with an inset bar and removed underline as well as colour.

Routes #/, #/day/<date>?q=<search> and #/job/<id> are built at 450-451 and parsed on load at 452-461; typing in search updates the URL with replaceState (597); onRoute(true) restores the view from the URL (936).

Views are hash routes handled on hashchange (930); the list scroll position is saved per day and restored on return (901, 916), the search stays in the URL (597), focus returns to the opened row (915-917), and an open dialog is closed (903).

The top bar link to today's jobs is always present (237); the job view, including its not-found and load-failed states, shows the back link (243, 711); the empty list offers a day link (536-538); errors offer Try again (577, 700, 704).
line 347: a native dialog element named by aria-labelledby=complete-title and described by aria-describedby, opened with showModal() (856).
No stepped flow: note, move and complete are each a single inline form or one dialog (310-321, 332-340, 347-355).
.btn min-height 48px (105); inputs min-height 48px (130); nav link, back link and phone link min-height 44px (81, 117, 179); job rows min-height 96px (152).
No position: fixed or sticky anywhere in the CSS (9-229); the header is in normal flow (65-68) and the only overlay is the native modal dialog.
